title: Universal Life Insurance Loan Accounting Computation Sheet: Settlement Interest
content:
Computation of the loan interest an owner of an Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance policy pays when settling loan interest in cash before it falls due.

## Statement of the computation

1. **Loan balance.** The loan balance used is the loan balance standing in the policy's activity history: the loan advances, plus the interest capitalized at earlier anniversaries, less the principal repaid.
2. **Days.** The days are the actual calendar days from the policy's loan interest paid-to date to the settlement date, the settlement date being the day the settlement is figured and booked.
3. **Rate.** The rate is the tier's standard loan charged rate, 5% a year on every tier (0.05).
4. **Settlement interest.** The settlement interest is the loan balance times the standard loan charged rate times the days, divided by 365, rounded to the cent once at the end. No intermediate figure is rounded.

## Reading the inputs

| Input | Where it is read |
|---|---|
| Loan advances | Every loan advance entry in the activity history |
| Interest capitalized | Every loan interest capitalization entry in the activity history |
| Principal repaid | The principal repaid on every loan repayment entry in the activity history |
| Loan interest paid-to date | The policy record |
| Settlement date | The day the settlement is booked |

## Worked figure (hypothetical)

Loan advances of $40000.00, interest capitalized of $1500.00 and principal repaid of $5000.00 give a loan balance of $36500.00. The paid-to date is 10 March 2025 and the settlement date 22 August 2025, 165 days later (21 in March, 30 in April, 31 in May, 30 in June, 31 in July and 22 in August).

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Loan balance | $36500.00 |
| Balance times 0.05 | $1825.00 a year |
| Times 165, divided by 365 | $825.00 |
| Rounded once to the cent | $825.00 |

With a balance of $36512.40 over the same days, the unrounded figure is $825.2803 and the settlement interest is $825.28.
